Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: deployment & PII questions for ACME pilot

Thanks Laura / Marissa —

We reviewed the MAP draft and have three primary constraints to resolve before the pilot kickoff:
1) Deployment mode: For the initial pilot we need either a VPC-hosted control plane with model execution in our VPC or an on-prem appliance. No public-hosted model endpoints are allowed.
2) Retention: Audit logs and request payloads may need to be retained for up to 7 years for our audit trail, but we could negotiate a shorter retention for raw inputs if they contain PII.
3) PII handling: We need confirmation on PII redaction support in-transit and whether Redwood can support token-level redaction or a pre-tokenization scrub pipeline.

Attached: acme-data-mapping.xlsx (sample column-level sensitivity).

Can you confirm what configuration options we can support, the timeline to deliver an on-prem package if needed, and any additional documentation we should share with our compliance team?

—Anna
Anna White
Director, DataOps — Acme Financial

Anna — thanks for the clear summary. High level responses below and then a proposed set of actions + owners.

- Deployment mode: We can support both VPC-hosted control plane (private networking + customer VPC connectors) and a fully on-prem package. On-prem delivery is possible but depends on the OS/kernel baseline and a brief validation window.
- Retention: We offer configurable retention policies. Default debug logs are 30 days; we can extend to your requested window for audit logs with a contract amendment. We recommend scoped retention rules so raw inputs with PII are retained for shorter windows and structured audit trails for longer.
- PII handling: Two options — (A) pre-ingest scrubbing in your environment (preferred), or (B) token-level redaction within our runtime using a PII classification plug-in. Option B requires a short engineering integration and a test vector set.

Proposed immediate MAP checkpoints (short):
- Tech validation call this Wed 11 AM PT (owner: Rishi) — confirm on-prem binary requirements and network port list.
- Compliance memo with retention proposal (owner: Marissa) — draft for Procurement and Compliance.
- PII pilot plan (owner: Laura) — decide between pre-ingest scrub vs runtime redaction and timeline.

Attaching a short one-pager MAP-week1.pdf with the timeline and meeting links.

Would Wednesday 11 AM PT work for your engineers?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett

Laura / team — quick technical notes ahead of Wed: 

1) On-prem package: We currently ship an on-prem runtime as a containerized bundle (validated on RHEL 8.6, Ubuntu 22.04) and an arm64/x86_64 build. Typical validation = 3 business days for networking + 2 days for perf smoke tests. Pre-requisites: outbound allowlist to Redwood’s control plane on TCP 443 for management (can be proxied), and internal port range 6000-6010 for worker heartbeat (configurable).

2) KMS/HSM: We support customer-managed KMS via standard KMIP and cloud KMS integrations. For HSM-backed keys we need admin contact and a short key-rotation policy doc.

3) Retention knobs: Audit logs are plumbed into our long-term store (S3-compatible). We can set retention at bucket-level up to 10 years; per-tenant policies are available. For raw input retention we can route to a separate bucket with 90-day default and legal-approved extensions.

4) PII scrub: Two practical flows — a) Pre-ingest: you perform field-level redaction and send only non-PII to Redwood (we provide a small SDK helper), or b) In-line classification: we can run a lightweight PII classifier in your VPC before model invocation that redacts tokens marked high-sensitivity. Option b requires test vectors and ~2 weeks eng time to validate at pilot scale.

I’ll bring a short checklist to Wed’s call; attaching redwood-onprem-checklist.pdf for your infra team to pre-check.

—Rishi

Laura / Rishi — thanks for the clarity. Wed 11 AM PT works. A few clarifications ahead of the call: 

- For compliance reasons we prefer the on-prem package for week 0 (kickoff + smoke) with the option to move to VPC-hosted control plane later. Our security team will want the container hash and an SBOM prior to installation.
- Retention: We can accept the split-bucket approach. For audit logs governance we need an SLA addendum to cover the extended retention and exportability of logs on exec.
- PII: We will attempt pre-ingest redaction for structured fields; however, there will be free-text inputs during the pilot. We are OK with the in-line classifier prototype for those free-text inputs provided data stays within our VPC and test vectors are strictly controlled.

I'll attach the procurement intake link and the compliance questionnaire in the Wed invite.
